entries.name: Listening at level 1, no transcript
entries.summary: Listen once, with no text to fall back on
entries.doesNotDo: It gives no partial credit. Without a transcript you cannot see which word you missed, only that you missed it.

entries.name: Narrow listening, one series, one speaker
entries.summary: One series, one voice, until the voice is easy
entries.doesNotDo: It tunes you to one voice. Getting comfortable with one speaker's rate and accent transfers to other speakers far less than it feels like it should.

entries.name: Repeated listening with support removal
entries.summary: The same clip three times, with less help each pass
entries.doesNotDo: It does not build volume, and by the third pass you are recalling the passage rather than parsing it.

entries.name: Partial dictation
entries.summary: Hear a sentence, fill in the words that were taken out
entries.doesNotDo: It measures the gaps and nothing else. The words you were handed tell you nothing about whether you would have heard them.

entries.name: Full dictation on paper
entries.summary: Hear a sentence, write the whole of it down
entries.doesNotDo: It is slow and it does not teach meaning. Ten minutes buys six sentences of sound-to-spelling, and comprehension is not what is being checked.

entries.name: Dictogloss — reconstruct rather than transcribe
entries.summary: Listen twice, then rebuild the passage from memory
entries.doesNotDo: It does not check that you heard the words. A good reconstruction can be built from gist plus grammar, which is the point and also the limitation.

entries.name: Listening faster (1.25×)
entries.summary: Something you already follow, a quarter faster
entries.doesNotDo: It adds no vocabulary. Speeding up material you already understand rehearses the parsing you have, not the words you lack.

entries.name: Background listening with no task
entries.summary: Leave it playing while you do something else
entries.doesNotDo: Honestly: barely anything. It is in the catalogue because learners ask about it, and the answer is that unattended sound produces almost no learning.
